title: Hiring for culture
header_line: My analysis of one book on habits. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What three things do you look for in a person you might hire?
I asked: when you hire, what are the top three things your attention goes to? A student said: attitude and perception, how much knowledge they have, and how they carry themselves.
A student said: if in the first conversation they start talking about negative things that happened to them, or bring up any negativity at all.

Another said: one of the worst things somebody can do to a culture is not be coachable, or be set in their ways, and automatically poke holes in a new process instead of embracing it. I sniff that out immediately.

A third said: look at how they were successful in a collaborative environment. Someone who says I did this and I executed that, but speaks little about collaboration, may single themselves out. He does not want to gain one person's skills and lose eight people on his team.
I asked each of them to name the signs of someone who could ruin the culture, and built the list from their answers.
What are your three characteristics and your three warning signs?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the three characteristics you look for.
Write a question that would show coachability.
Write a question that would show collaboration.
Write how you will check a candidate's answers.

check.q: What did a student say is one of the worst things for a culture?
What did a student look for in an interview?
What did a student say about negativity in the first conversation?

recap: Hire for attitude, coachability and collaboration. Know your warning signs.
